issues.description: The template Stock.findStockIngredient method signature expects two parameters (String name, boolean caseSensitive), but the problem specification UML and the solution use a single-parameter signature findStockIngredient(String). Furthermore, other methods in the template Stock (add, take) and the commented Main invocation call findStockIngredient(String) with only one parameter. This inconsistency causes compilation errors in the template and contradicts the intended API described in the problem and shown in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification and solution by providing a single-argument method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either change the existing method signature to the single-parameter form, or add an overloaded helper method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the two-parameter variant (e.g., calling findStockIngredient(name, true)). Also ensure internal calls in Stock (add, take) and Main use the single-argument form so the template compiles and aligns with the problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method (single String parameter), but the template Stock.java defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with a caseSensitive flag. This mismatch makes it unclear for students which method signature to use when following the exercise: problem examples and other template code (e.g., add/take calls) use a single-argument form, while the template only provides a two-argument variant. It creates a direct mapping/compilation confusion and extra cognitive load when students try to implement SealSaloon functionality that relies on finding ingredients by name.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Stock.java to provide the single-argument method signature findStockIngredient(String name) as specified in the problem (and implemented in the solution). Either replace the two-argument variant with the single-argument one, or add an overloaded single-argument method that delegates to the two-argument version (e.g., findStockIngredient(name) calls findStockIngredient(name, false)). This will align template, problem statement, and solution and remove ambiguity for students.
